body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
[ARBA: ARBA00023239](https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00023239)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel FBgn0037656 | CG11986 (Q9VHI3)

* **Description of issue**
This protein gets 'lyase activity' because of this:
[ARBA: ARBA00023239](https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00023239) -> [#Lyase](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0456) (KW-0456) -> [lyase activity (GO:0016829)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0016829)

This seems to because of this InterPro/Panther match:
[IPR003738](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR003738)
[IPR036590](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR036590)
[PTHR13604:SF0](https://www.pantherdb.org/panther/family.do?clsAccession=PTHR13604:SF0)

But I don't see any evidence for 'lyase activity' there.
IPR003738 is "SOS response associated peptidase (SRAP)" (no GO annotations)
IPR036590 is "SOS response associated peptidase-like" (no GO annotations) - note this is just the parent to IPR003738!

author: Antonialock
body: oh, e coli had EC 4.-.-.- (Lyases) from https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821365, which was propagated to other entries. the paper says Reaction scheme Based on our results, we propose a potential reaction scheme for DPC formation between yedK and AP sites in ssDNA (Figure [7A](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821365/#F7); [26](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821365/#B26),[27](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821365/#B27)). The thiol group of the catalytic Cys2 residue of yedK is easily deprotonated by its α-amino group to form a thiolate anion that is poised for catalysis. The AP site sugar moiety is in equilibrium between its cyclic furanose and open-chain aldehyde forms ([20](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821365/#B20)). The Cys2 thiolate anion attacks the AP site C1’ position to form a covalent bond. The Cys2 α-amino group proton then transfers to the oxygen which is stabilized by the Asn75 side chain. The O4’ rotates to a new position and interacts with the His160 side chain. The Cys2 α-amino group then attacks the C1’ position and transfers a proton to the hydroxyl group to release a water molecule, meanwhile forming a covalent bond with the C1’ atom. Thus, a thiazolidine linkage is formed between the AP site C1’ atom and the Cys2 amino and thiol groups. The Glu105 side chain carboxyl stabilizes the thiazolidine linkage via a strong hydrogen bond with its amine group. I will ask Sylvain about whether he thinks 4.-.-.- is correct for this
